annotations.description: With Dragon's Rage Channeler and Monastery Swiftspear in hand, the optimal turn 1 play is to lead with Mishra's Bauble first (it's a free 0-mana artifact), then play Mountain, then cast Dragon's Rage Channeler. Casting Bauble before DRC means the DRC's surveil trigger fires when you cast noncreature spells later, but more importantly, playing Bauble first gets an artifact into the graveyard (after sacrificing it) to help enable Delirium faster. By playing Mountain first without casting Bauble, the player loses the opportunity to sequence optimally. The correct line is: cast Mishra's Bauble (free), activate and sacrifice it targeting opponent, play Mountain, then cast Dragon's Rage Channeler. This gets an artifact in the graveyard immediately and starts the card draw process.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as the first action of the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mishra's Bauble first (0 mana, can be cast before land drop), activate and sacrifice it, then play Mountain, then cast Dragon's Rage Channeler. This sequences the artifact into the graveyard earlier for Delirium and triggers DRC's surveil if any further noncreature spells are cast.

annotations.description: Casting Monastery Swiftspear before Mishra's Bauble wastes a free Prowess trigger. Bauble costs 0 mana and is a noncreature spell, so casting it first (or after Swiftspear but before combat) would give Swiftspear +1/+1 until end of turn, allowing it to attack as a 2/3 instead of 1/2. The correct sequence is: cast Swiftspear, then cast Bauble to trigger Prowess, then attack for 2 instead of 1. Alternatively, casting Bauble first then Swiftspear is fine too since Swiftspear has haste - but the key is Bauble should be cast after Swiftspear and before combat. Since Swiftspear was cast in precombat main, there's still time to cast Bauble before attacking, but the decision point here is just about which creature to play - and Swiftspear is correct over DRC. The real sequencing issue is whether Bauble gets cast before combat. However, looking at the decision itself (choosing Swiftspear over DRC), Swiftspear is actually the right creature to deploy on turn 1 with haste. The only minor issue is that casting Mishra's Bauble first would have been free and could set up the Prowess trigger, but since Bauble can still be cast after this in the same main phase, this specific choice isn't necessarily wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Monastery Swiftspear with R mana on turn 1
annotations.betterLine: This is actually reasonable - Swiftspear is the right creature. The player can still cast Bauble before combat for the Prowess trigger.

annotations.description: The player is fetching a land (likely from Wooded Foothills, which searches for a Mountain or Forest). With the opponent at 16 life and the player at 18 life holding aggressive creatures and Lightning Bolt, every point of life matters but so does mana efficiency. However, the player already has red sources covered by Mountain and could benefit from having additional blue mana for future Spell Pierces or other blue spells. That said, fetching basic Mountain preserves 2 life (or avoids entering tapped) and the player already has blue from Thundering Falls and Steam Vents. The basic Mountain is almost certainly correct here since they have plenty of blue sources already and don't need to pay 2 life for another dual land.

annotations.description: Casting Monastery Swiftspear before combat is suboptimal sequencing. With haste, Swiftspear can attack this turn regardless. By casting it pre-combat, Kimi25 loses the opportunity to cast noncreature spells (like Lightning Bolt) before declaring attacks to trigger prowess on the Swiftspear during combat. More importantly, casting creatures before combat when holding combat tricks (Lightning Bolt) reveals information unnecessarily and doesn't leverage the haste advantage properly. The optimal line would be to cast Swiftspear, then cast additional noncreature spells to pump it via prowess before attacking. However, the bigger sequencing concern is that casting the creature first telegraphs the attack plan to the opponent, and if they had interaction, it gives them more information. That said, casting Swiftspear first does allow subsequent noncreature spells to trigger prowess, so there's some logic to it. The real issue is whether Dragon's Rage Channeler should have been cast first instead - DRC would benefit from surveil triggers from noncreature spells and with 4 card types already in graveyard (creature, sorcery, land, land - actually Slickshot Show-Off is creature, Preordain is sorcery, Bloodstained Mire and Wooded Foothills are lands - that's only 3 types: creature, sorcery, land), DRC needs one more type. Mishra's Bauble could be sacrificed to put an artifact in the graveyard for delirium, making DRC a 3/3 flyer. But Swiftspear with haste is reasonable for immediate pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Monastery Swiftspear as the first spell in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon's Rage Channeler first (to set up surveil and potential delirium with Mishra's Bauble sacrifice adding artifact to graveyard for a 3/3 flyer), or alternatively cast Swiftspear but follow up with noncreature spells before combat to maximize prowess triggers

annotations.description: Kimi25 Truth has a Monastery Swiftspear on board and 4 lands (one tapped Mountain, Thundering Falls, two Steam Vents). They have Lightning Bolt, Dragon's Rage Channeler, Slickshot Show-Off, and Cori-Steel Cutter in hand. The opponent has Gran-Gran, Emperor of Bones, and Psychic Frog - all dangerous creatures that will generate incremental value. Passing without casting anything and skipping the attack phase wastes an entire turn of development. At minimum, Dragon's Rage Channeler should be deployed (it costs R, and there are untapped lands available) to start surveilling toward delirium. Lightning Bolt could remove a key threat like Psychic Frog or Emperor of Bones. Slickshot Show-Off could be plotted for a future explosive turn. Instead, the player did literally nothing - no spells, no attacks with Monastery Swiftspear - giving the opponent a free turn to develop their board and generate value with Emperor of Bones and Psychic Frog.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells and skipped the attack phase entirely, wasting a full turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon's Rage Channeler (R) to develop the board and enable surveil. Consider using Lightning Bolt on Psychic Frog or Emperor of Bones to prevent value generation. At minimum, attack with Monastery Swiftspear - casting noncreature spells first would trigger prowess for extra damage. Plot Slickshot Show-Off for a future alpha strike. Doing nothing with 3 untapped lands and relevant spells in hand against an opponent building a threatening board is a significant waste of tempo.

annotations.description: At end of opponent's turn, Mishra's Bauble should be activated since it provides free information (look at top of library) and a free card draw next upkeep. There is zero cost and no reason to hold it - the artifact is just sitting unused on the battlefield.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Bauble targeting either player's library to get free information and a card draw next upkeep. annotations.description: Casting Thoughtseize before playing a land and before combat is a sequencing consideration. The opponent has only Monastery Swiftspear on board with one untapped land (Mountain is tapped), while MiniMx Gramps has Emperor of Bones and Psychic Frog. More importantly, Thoughtseize costs 2 life (going from 16 to 14), and the opponent has an aggressive deck. Playing a fetch land first (Polluted Delta, Scalding Tarn, or Bloodstained Mire) would enable revolt for Fatal Push, which could kill creatures with mana value 4 or less. Additionally, if the opponent's hand is mostly lands or low-impact cards, the Thoughtseize may not be worth the life loss at this stage. However, getting information and stripping a key card before combat and before the opponent untaps fully is reasonable. The main concern is sequencing - playing a fetch land first before Thoughtseize would be better since it doesn't cost anything and keeps revolt available for Fatal Push if needed during combat or in response to something.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thoughtseize before playing a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play a fetch land first (e.g., Bloodstained Mire or Polluted Delta) to ensure the land drop isn't missed, then cast Thoughtseize. This preserves the option to crack the fetch for revolt-enabled Fatal Push if needed later.

annotations.description: Thoughtseize is on the stack targeting Kimi25 Truth, and they're being given priority to respond. They have Lightning Bolt which could target Emperor of Bones or Psychic Frog (both serious threats), and Mishra's Bauble which is a free activation to get information and a card draw next upkeep. Activating Mishra's Bauble here costs nothing - it's a 0-mana artifact that sacrifices to look at a card and draw next upkeep. Declining a pure-upside free ability is a clear mistake. The Bauble activation would also put an artifact in the graveyard (adding to card types for potential delirium on Dragon's Rage Channeler) and trigger the sacrifice which could enable revolt for Fatal Push if they had one. There's no reason not to activate it.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Mishra's Bauble or cast Lightning Bolt in response to Thoughtseize, allowing the opponent to see all four cards in hand including Lightning Bolt and Slickshot Show-Off.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Bauble (free, pure upside - draws a card next upkeep, puts artifact in graveyard for delirium). Could also consider casting Lightning Bolt on Emperor of Bones or Psychic Frog to hide it from Thoughtseize's reveal, though that's more debatable.

Lightning Bolt has no clean answer from Gramps' hand and threatens to kill key creatures (Gran-Gran, Emperor of Bones, Psychic Frog are all within Bolt range) while also representing 3 damage to face.

annotations.description: Casting Cori-Steel Cutter (a non-creature spell) before combat is suboptimal when Monastery Swiftspear is on the battlefield. Swiftspear has prowess, so casting noncreature spells before combat would pump it +1/+1 for the attack. However, the bigger issue is sequencing: casting the equipment before combat telegraphs the plan and gives the opponent information. More importantly, if the player plans to cast a second spell this turn to trigger Cori-Steel Cutter's flurry ability (creating a 1/1 Monk token that can be equipped), they should consider whether Lightning Bolt targeting the opponent or a blocker before combat might be more impactful. The Cori-Steel Cutter does trigger prowess on Swiftspear, which is good before combat, but casting Dragon's Rage Channeler first (a creature, no prowess trigger) and then the equipment as the second spell would trigger flurry and create a token. The sequencing of casting a noncreature spell before combat is actually correct for prowess on Swiftspear, but the player should consider whether Lightning Bolt (which also triggers prowess AND deals 3 damage or removes a blocker) would be better as the pre-combat spell, saving the equipment for post-combat or as the second spell for flurry.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Cori-Steel Cutter as the first spell in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Bolt targeting a key blocker (Emperor of Bones or Psychic Frog) or the opponent before combat to trigger prowess on Monastery Swiftspear, then attack, then cast Cori-Steel Cutter post-combat. Alternatively, cast Dragon's Rage Channeler first (creature, no prowess), then Cori-Steel Cutter as second spell to trigger flurry and create a hasty equipped Monk token for combat.

annotations.description: Casting Cori-Steel Cutter (a noncreature spell) before combat is suboptimal when Monastery Swiftspear is on the battlefield. The prowess trigger gives Swiftspear +1/+1 until end of turn, meaning that power boost is wasted if cast precombat without then attacking. However, Swiftspear likely will attack this turn, so the timing isn't terrible - but the bigger issue is sequencing. Casting the equipment precombat commits mana and reveals information. More importantly, Lightning Bolt could potentially be more impactful - for example, bolting Psychic Frog or Emperor of Bones before combat to clear blockers. Additionally, casting Dragon's Rage Channeler first (a creature) wouldn't trigger prowess, so casting it before the noncreature spells would be better sequencing if planning to cast both. The Cutter's Flurry ability triggers on the second spell each turn, so casting DRC first then Cutter would create a 1/1 Monk token with the equipment auto-attached, giving a hasty 2/2 trampler. This sequencing was missed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Cori-Steel Cutter as the first spell of the turn in precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon's Rage Channeler first (as the first spell), then cast Cori-Steel Cutter as the second spell to trigger Flurry, creating a 1/1 Monk token with prowess that auto-attaches the equipment (becoming a 2/2 with trample and haste). This also triggers Monastery Swiftspear's prowess twice and DRC's surveil. Then attack with the hasty Monk token, Swiftspear, and DRC.

annotations.description: Psychic Frog is one of MiniMx Gramps' best creatures - it generates card advantage on combat damage, can grow with discards, and can gain flying. Trading it for a Monastery Swiftspear (which is just a 1/1 haste with prowess, currently 2/3 from a pump) is a poor exchange. The player has 14 life and can afford to take 2 damage. Psychic Frog is significantly more valuable than 2 life points, especially when the player has cards to discard to it and Emperor of Bones to generate board presence. Additionally, Psychic Frog dying doesn't trigger Revolt for Fatal Push since it's the opponent's creature killing it during their attack - wait, actually it's the opponent's turn... No, looking again, this is MiniMx Gramps' combat phase but Monastery Swiftspear is tapped and attacking. Actually, re-reading: it's MiniMx Gramps' turn in combat, being asked to select blockers, meaning the opponent attacked with Monastery Swiftspear. Taking 2 damage to preserve Psychic Frog would have been significantly better.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Monastery Swiftspear with Psychic Frog, trading away a key card advantage creature to save 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Take the 2 damage from Monastery Swiftspear (going to 12 life), preserving Psychic Frog which is far more valuable as a card advantage engine and win condition.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones exiles a card from a graveyard at the beginning of combat, and when +1/+1 counters are put on it (via Adapt 2 for 1B), it can reanimate a creature card exiled with it. The player exiled Thoughtseize, which is a sorcery and cannot be put onto the battlefield as a creature. Meanwhile, Monastery Swiftspear is available in the opponent's graveyard - a creature card that could actually be reanimated with Emperor of Bones' ability if they later Adapt. Even Slickshot Show-Off would be a much better target as a creature that could be reanimated. Exiling a non-creature card wastes the reanimation potential of Emperor of Bones.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Thoughtseize (a sorcery) with Emperor of Bones' trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Monastery Swiftspear or Slickshot Show-Off - creature cards that Emperor of Bones could actually reanimate when it gets +1/+1 counters via Adapt.

annotations.description: MiniMx Gramps had Emperor of Bones' beginning of combat trigger exile Thoughtseize (which was already exiled or a card in graveyard), but more importantly, they skipped their attack entirely despite having Psychic Frog (1/2) and potentially Emperor of Bones (2/2) and Gran-Gran on the board against an opponent with no creatures (only Cori-Steel Cutter equipment and Mishra's Bauble). The opponent at 16 life has no blockers, so attacking with available creatures would deal free damage. Additionally, Psychic Frog draws a card on combat damage to a player, making the attack even more valuable. Skipping the attack phase entirely wastes significant value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat and then skipped the attack entirely, dealing 0 damage to an opponent with no blockers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Psychic Frog (and possibly Emperor of Bones and Gran-Gran) into the empty board. Psychic Frog connecting draws a card, and free damage brings the opponent closer to lethal range. Could also discard Unearth to pump Psychic Frog before damage for extra damage and to fuel the graveyard for Abhorrent Oculus.

annotations.description: Activating Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 in the postcombat main phase means the reanimated Dragon's Rage Channeler (which gains haste) cannot attack this turn, and it will be sacrificed at the next end step. The haste and the creature are essentially wasted. DRC is only a 1/1 without delirium (graveyard has only 2 card types).
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 postcombat, reanimating DRC as a 1/1 that can't attack and dies at end step.
annotations.betterLine: Wait to activate Adapt 2 on next turn during or before combat, so the reanimated creature with haste can actually attack. This turn, could pass or use mana on Psychic Frog's discard ability if beneficial.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Emperor of Bones's Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B} with mana available. This would permanently make Emperor of Bones a 4/4 (from 2/2) and put the exiled Dragon's Rage Channeler onto the battlefield with haste and a finality counter. While DRC would be sacrificed at end step since it's postcombat, the permanent +2/+2 on Emperor of Bones is significant value that was left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using any abilities, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones's Adapt 2 for {1}{B} to permanently make it a 4/4 and get a temporary Dragon's Rage Channeler. Could also consider discarding Unearth (no valid targets in graveyard) to Psychic Frog for a +1/+1 counter.

annotations.description: Failed to use Adapt 2 on Emperor of Bones at end of turn with 2 untapped mana ({1}{B} available from Undercity Sewers + Blood Crypt). This would permanently make Emperor a 4/4 and put Dragon's Rage Channeler (exiled with Emperor) onto the battlefield as a temporary creature/blocker. The mana would have gone unused otherwise.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority at end of turn without activating any abilities, wasting 2 available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B}, making it a permanent 4/4 and getting a temporary Dragon's Rage Channeler as a blocker for the opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Passed on Emperor of Bones' beginning of combat exile trigger when opponent's graveyard contained valuable creatures (Monastery Swiftspear, two Slickshot Show-Offs). Exiling a creature could set up a future adapt + reanimate play. Also missed opportunity to use Psychic Frog's discard ability (discarding Unearth, which has no valid targets since no creatures are in graveyard) to get a +1/+1 counter for extra damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using any abilities or casting any spells during their own precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Use Emperor of Bones' combat trigger to exile a Slickshot Show-Off or Monastery Swiftspear from opponent's graveyard, and consider discarding the dead Unearth to Psychic Frog for a +1/+1 counter before combat.

annotations.description: Discarded Mishra's Bauble instead of Lava Dart. Lava Dart has flashback (sacrifice a Mountain) so discarding it loses almost no value - it can still be cast from the graveyard. Mishra's Bauble is a free cantrip that also triggers prowess on Monastery Swiftspears, providing meaningful value. The player even recognized this in their reasoning ('Or maybe Lava Dart since I can flash it') but chose Bauble anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Mishra's Bauble
annotations.betterLine: Discard Lava Dart, which retains full utility from the graveyard via its flashback cost (sacrifice a Mountain). This preserves Mishra's Bauble as a free prowess trigger and cantrip for future turns.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones exiles a card from a graveyard at the beginning of combat, and when it gets +1/+1 counters (via Adapt 2), it can reanimate a creature exiled with it. Slickshot Show-Off is a 1/2 flying haste creature that gets +2/+0 per noncreature spell cast - decent but temporary. However, Monastery Swiftspear is also available in the opponent's graveyard. The key consideration is what MiniMx Gramps plans to do with the exiled card. If they adapt Emperor of Bones (costs 1B), they get to put the exiled creature onto the battlefield with haste (sacrificed at end step). Slickshot Show-Off as a 1/2 flyer with haste is reasonable, but Monastery Swiftspear (1/2 haste with prowess) is comparable. The real question is whether exiling Slickshot Show-Off from the opponent's graveyard is more about denying a future Unearth/reanimation target or about using it yourself. Given that the opponent plays red aggro and might not have graveyard recursion, and that MiniMx Gramps has Unearth in hand (which only targets their own graveyard), this is a reasonable defensive exile choice since Slickshot Show-Off is one of the more dangerous cards the opponent could potentially recur. The choice is defensible but exiling Monastery Swiftspear (another threat) would be roughly equivalent.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Slickshot Show-Off from opponent's graveyard with Emperor of Bones' combat trigger
annotations.betterLine: This is a close call - Slickshot Show-Off is a reasonable choice both for denial and potential reanimation via Adapt. Could argue Monastery Swiftspear is slightly better to reanimate (prowess synergy with spells in hand), but the difference is marginal.

annotations.description: With no opposing creatures on the battlefield, Psychic Frog can attack freely. Discarding Unearth to Psychic Frog before attacks would have pumped it to 2/3 (dealing 1 extra damage and still drawing a card on hit), while also positioning Unearth in the graveyard for future use as a reanimation spell. The pass gave up a free point of damage and graveyard setup.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Psychic Frog's discard ability before declaring attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Unearth to Psychic Frog to put a +1/+1 counter on it, then attack with the pumped Frog (and potentially other creatures) for extra damage while setting up Unearth in the graveyard for later.

annotations.description: With the opponent at 5 life, discarding Abhorrent Oculus to Psychic Frog's ability would permanently grow it with a +1/+1 counter. Abhorrent Oculus requires exiling 6 cards from graveyard to cast, and MiniMx Gramps only has 4 cards in graveyard, making it currently uncastable. The extra point of power on Psychic Frog could be critical for closing out the game against an opponent at 5 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities, keeping Abhorrent Oculus in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Abhorrent Oculus to Psychic Frog's ability to put a permanent +1/+1 counter on it, since Oculus is likely uncastable and the extra power helps close out the game with opponent at 5 life.

annotations.description: Failed to play Scalding Tarn from hand when they had a land drop available. Playing a land is free and provides additional mana for future turns. Moreover, Scalding Tarn can be cracked to add a card to the graveyard, helping toward the 6-card graveyard requirement for the two Abhorrent Oculus in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing Scalding Tarn, missing their land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn to make their land drop, preserving access to additional mana and a future graveyard card for Abhorrent Oculus.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Truth is at 5 life facing a tapped-out opponent at 11 life, with Lightning Bolt (3 damage), Lava Dart (1 damage, plus flashback for another 1 = 2 total), Unholy Heat (2 damage to face if targeting player... wait, Unholy Heat only hits creatures/planeswalkers). Let me recalculate: Lightning Bolt (3 to face) + Lava Dart (1 to face) + Lava Dart flashback sacrificing Mountain (1 to face) = 5 damage from burn. Plus two Monastery Swiftspears and Dragon's Rage Channeler can be deployed. With the opponent completely tapped out, this is the turn to deploy threats and start racing. The opponent has Psychic Frog, Emperor of Bones, and Gran-Gran that will attack next turn for lethal if uncontested. Passing the turn with a hand full of spells while at 5 life against an opponent who can attack for lethal is catastrophic. At minimum, deploying creatures as blockers is essential for survival, and burning the opponent brings them into kill range.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, then skipped attack, effectively doing nothing on a critical turn.
annotations.betterLine: Deploy Dragon's Rage Channeler and both Monastery Swiftspears as blockers/attackers. Cast noncreature spells to trigger prowess. Lightning Bolt the opponent's face (opponent to 8). Use Lava Dart to face (opponent to 7), flashback Lava Dart sacrificing Mountain (opponent to 6). The prowess triggers on Swiftspears from these noncreature spells would make them formidable attackers/blockers. This develops a board presence for blocking the opponent's lethal attack while putting significant pressure on their life total.

annotations.description: Discarded Preordain over the second copy of Cori-Steel Cutter when one Cori-Steel Cutter is already on the battlefield. Preordain is a 1-mana cantrip that provides card selection to find the right cards to close the game, while a second Cori-Steel Cutter is redundant with the first copy already in play.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Preordain
annotations.betterLine: Discard the second Cori-Steel Cutter since one is already on the battlefield, keeping Preordain for efficient card selection to find the right sequencing to close out the game from 5 life.

annotations.description: Declined Emperor of Bones' beginning of combat exile trigger, which is a free 'up to one' ability with no downside. Could have exiled Monastery Swiftspear from opponent's graveyard to set up potential adapt value. With the opponent at 5 life and no blockers, the adapt line (making Emperor 4/4 and getting DRC with haste) would provide massive overkill damage. Even without adapt, exiling a creature is pure upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without using Emperor of Bones' combat exile trigger
annotations.betterLine: Use Emperor of Bones' combat trigger to exile Monastery Swiftspear from opponent's graveyard (free value), then consider adapting Emperor of Bones for additional damage and DRC with haste

annotations.description: When manifesting dread (from Abhorrent Oculus's trigger), you look at the top two cards and put one face-down as a 2/2 creature and the other into your graveyard. Putting Abhorrent Oculus into the graveyard wastes a powerful card - it's a 5/5 flyer that could be manifested face-down and then turned face up for its mana cost (though it requires exiling 6 cards from graveyard as additional cost, which complicates flipping). However, Scalding Tarn as the manifest can never be turned face up (it's not a creature card), so it's just a 2/2 forever. Abhorrent Oculus as the manifest at least has the theoretical upside of being flipped into a 5/5 flyer if conditions allow. Additionally, Scalding Tarn in the graveyard would have been more useful - it's a land that does nothing as a 2/2, while putting it in the graveyard adds a land card type to the graveyard (though land is already potentially covered). The key issue is that manifesting the Oculus gives a body that could potentially become a 5/5 flyer, while manifesting the Tarn gives a permanently vanilla 2/2.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to manifest Scalding Tarn face-down (permanently a 2/2) and put Abhorrent Oculus into the graveyard.
annotations.betterLine: Manifest Abhorrent Oculus face-down (can potentially be turned face up as a 5/5 flyer) and put Scalding Tarn into the graveyard.

annotations.description: Discarded Psychic Frog instead of a redundant Abhorrent Oculus. Psychic Frog is a strong 2-mana value creature that can be replayed. With only 5 cards in graveyard, discarding either card brings it to 6, enabling one Abhorrent Oculus cast. Discarding a redundant Oculus (can't cast both anyway due to graveyard exile requirement) preserves the more flexible Psychic Frog for future use.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Psychic Frog to pump the attacking Psychic Frog
annotations.betterLine: Discard an Abhorrent Oculus instead, preserving Psychic Frog as a replayable threat while still enabling the remaining Oculus cast from the 6-card graveyard

annotations.description: Lightning Bolt in the graveyard has no way to be cast without specific recursion, while Lava Dart has flashback (sacrifice a Mountain) and the opponent controls a Mountain. Exiling Lava Dart would remove an actual live threat from the graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Lightning Bolt from graveyard with Emperor of Bones trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Lava Dart instead, since it has flashback and can be cast from the graveyard by sacrificing the opponent's Mountain for 1 damage plus potential prowess triggers.

annotations.description: By manifesting Archon of Cruelty (which costs 8 mana to flip face-up, very unlikely), they put Persist into the graveyard where it's a useless sorcery. They should have manifested Persist (a sorcery that can NEVER be flipped face-up anyway, so it's always just a 2/2) and put Archon of Cruelty into the graveyard, where it could be reanimated by a future Persist draw for a game-winning ETB trigger against an opponent at 5 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Manifested Archon of Cruelty face-down, sending Persist to graveyard
annotations.betterLine: Manifest Persist face-down (permanent 2/2 either way since sorceries can't flip) and put Archon of Cruelty in graveyard as a reanimation target

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Abhorrent Oculus with only 5 cards in graveyard (needs 6 to exile as additional cost), and with insufficient mana (only Blood Crypt untapped, providing B/R, while the spell costs {2}{U}). This is an illegal play that the game engine apparently allowed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Abhorrent Oculus during combat with insufficient graveyard cards and mana
annotations.betterLine: Pass through combat and hold up Fatal Push with Blood Crypt for the opponent's turn, maintaining defensive options against the opponent at 5 life

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones' combat trigger exiles a card that can potentially be put onto the battlefield attacking when Emperor attacks. Exiling Preordain (a sorcery) wastes this opportunity. Monastery Swiftspear was available as a creature to exile, which could be reanimated attacking for extra damage against an opponent at 5 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Preordain (a sorcery) with Emperor of Bones' trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Monastery Swiftspear to potentially put it onto the battlefield tapped and attacking via Emperor of Bones' attack trigger, adding extra damage against the opponent at 5 life.

annotations.description: Manifested Bloodstained Mire (a land that can never be turned face up) instead of Psychic Frog (a creature that could be flipped for just {U}{B}). The manifest of a land is permanently stuck as a vanilla 2/2, while manifesting the Frog preserves the option to flip it into a real threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Manifested Bloodstained Mire face-down and put Psychic Frog into the graveyard.
annotations.betterLine: Manifest Psychic Frog face-down (can be flipped for {U}{B} into a 1/2 with all abilities) and put Bloodstained Mire into the graveyard where it has minimal utility.

annotations.description: The player declined or mishandled the manifest dread trigger from Abhorrent Oculus, which is a pure-upside ability. The correct choice was to manifest Psychic Frog face-down (which can be flipped face-up for just {U}{B} since it's a creature card) and put Bitter Triumph into the graveyard. The reasoning 'I don't control this action' is incorrect - this is MiniMx Gramps' own Abhorrent Oculus trigger and they absolutely control this choice.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose False / declined the manifest dread selection
annotations.betterLine: Manifest Psychic Frog face-down (can be turned face up for {U}{B} to get a 1/2 with upside) and put Bitter Triumph into the graveyard.

annotations.description: Fetching basic Island instead of Undercity Sewers misses the surveil 1 trigger that could put a 6th card into the graveyard, which is needed to enable casting Abhorrent Oculus (requires exiling 6 cards from graveyard, currently only 5 there). Since it's already the combat phase with most lands tapped, the 'enters tapped' downside of Undercity Sewers is negligible - both lands would be untapped next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Island
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Undercity Sewers to get surveil 1, potentially putting a 6th card in graveyard to enable Abhorrent Oculus next turn. The dual-color flexibility (U/B) is also better than just U.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 5 life. MiniMx Gramps has delirium active (land, instant, sorcery, creature in graveyard - 4+ types). Unholy Heat with delirium deals 6 damage to a creature or planeswalker, not directly to face - but it's still a powerful removal spell. More importantly, Lava Dart can deal 1 damage to face and be flashed back for another 1, helping close the game. Dragon's Rage Channeler is a strong threat. Preordain is just card selection when the game should be about closing out quickly at this life total differential.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Preordain - a cantrip for card selection
annotations.betterLine: Should have taken Dragon's Rage Channeler as an additional threat to pressure the opponent at 5 life, or Lava Dart for flexible burn damage (1 + 1 flashback to face). With the opponent at 5 life, adding board pressure or direct damage is more valuable than card selection.

annotations.description: This is Emperor of Bones' beginning of combat trigger, which exiles a card from a graveyard to fuel its ability to cast creatures from exile. The chosen card 'Faithless Looting' is not listed among the available choices shown (which include cards like Lava Dart, Monastery Swiftspear, Thoughtseize, Preordain, etc.). The reasoning also incorrectly references 'Expressive Iteration' which isn't involved. More importantly, the optimal exile target should be a creature card like Monastery Swiftspear (from opponent's graveyard) since Emperor of Bones can cast exiled creature cards, making a creature far more valuable to exile than a sorcery like Faithless Looting.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Faithless Looting with Emperor of Bones' trigger, apparently confused about the source of the ability.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Monastery Swiftspear from opponent's graveyard, as Emperor of Bones can cast exiled creature cards, giving you access to a hasty attacker. Alternatively, exile a relevant creature to deny graveyard synergies.

annotations.description: Casting Abhorrent Oculus during combat with seemingly insufficient graveyard cards (only 5 visible, need 6) and only 1 untapped land (Blood Crypt) when the card costs {2}{U}. The reasoning also incorrectly describes the card's ability as generating treasures when it actually manifest dreads. With opponent at 5 life, focusing on closing the game with existing attackers and holding Fatal Push for defense may be more reliable.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Abhorrent Oculus during combat phase
annotations.betterLine: Pass through combat, hold up Fatal Push with Blood Crypt mana for defensive purposes, and look to close the game with existing board threats next turn

annotations.description: Discarded Polluted Delta instead of the basic Swamp. Polluted Delta is strictly better to keep because it enables revolt for Fatal Push (in hand), can fetch either Island or Swamp for color flexibility, and thins the deck. The basic Swamp provides none of these advantages.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Polluted Delta to pump Psychic Frog, keeping Thoughtseize and Swamp.
annotations.betterLine: Discard the basic Swamp instead, preserving Polluted Delta for its revolt synergy with Fatal Push and superior utility.
